newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Jan 20.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- BP SIGNS $1 BILLION CONTRACT TO PIPE N SEA GAS TO EUROPE
British Petroleum has agreed to export $1 billion worth of gas from its North Sea fields to its partners in a new North sea pipeline link.
-- DIAL-A-PENSION PLAN SHRUGS OFF HERMES DELAY

Liberty International Holdings is launching PensionStore, becoming the first company to specialise solely in selling pensions by telephone. The launch will go ahead without the 1.5 billion pounds stg backing British Telecom pension scheme and its fund manager, Hermes, promised last October.
-- GOVERNMENT WELCOME FOR EU MOVE ON CASH TRANSFER

The government welcomed European Union legislation to protect bank customers when sending money abroad. On amounts of up to 50,000 ecu, or nearly 40,000 pounds stg, banks will not be allowed to levy transfer fees at both ends of the transaction without the customer's agreement and the originating bank will be forced to pay interest if the money arrives late.
THE TIMES
-- AIRTOURS SHARE SCHEME ANGERS PENSION FUND ADVISERS

Shareholders in holiday company Airtours have been asked to reject the report and accounts at the company's annual meeting on Thursday due to a share scheme that is potentially worth 3.7 million pounds stg to the first four directors to benefit. Pensions & Investments Research Consultants is annoyed that a new long-term incentive plan was introduced by Airtours in September without seeking shareholders' approval, which was a breach of the Greenbury code on executive pay.
-- HESELTINE AND BLAIR PITCH FOR BUSINESS VOTE

The Government will clash with Labour over British business, when Michael Heseltine, Deputy Prime Minister, and opposition leader Tony Blair speak on the same platform in an appeal for business votes.
-- THAMESLINK POISED TO ENTER PRIVATE SECTOR NETWORK
The most lucrative of the seven remaining rail franchises, Thameslink, will go into private hands this week after months of speculation pushed the shares of the four bidders to record highs.
THE GUARDIAN
-- SIX MILLION POUNDS AT CENTRE OF HORLICK ROW

Nicola Horlick, who resigned last week from Morgan Grenfell Asset Management claiming constructive dismissal, is thought to have assets in an offshore financial haven of up to six million pounds stg. It is this account that will form the centrepiece in any litigation between the City fund-manager and her former employer.
-- FORD THREAT TO SHUT CAR PLANT UNLESS IT GETS AID
Ford's Halewood assembly plant in Merseyside will close with the loss of 4,500 jobs unless it gets a government grant towards the cost of producing a new vehicle there, the car group has said.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- MORGAN PREPARES OFFENSIVE TO HOLD ON TO CLIENTS

Morgan Grenfell Asset Management's top fund managers are to fight to stop their business breaking down this week after clients' worries over the stability of the operation were rekindled by the departure of Nicola Horlick. They will also seek to quash rumours that the bank's head office in Frankfurt is angry over the way the London management handled Mrs Horlick's resignation.
-- THE 34 BILLION POUND TAX HIKES LABOUR COULD IMPOSE

NatWest Markets the investment bankers is to publish new research speculating a plausible list of 34 billion pounds stg of tax increases that a Labour government could introduce in the lifetime of a parliament.
